newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Swiss Glencore wins Bulgaria 53,000 t wheat tender.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Glencore wins Bulgaria 53,000 t wheat tender.

text.p: The Swiss firm Glencore won a third wheat import tender for 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat at $156.35 per tonne, deputy agriculture minister Valya Savcheva said on Tuesday.
"Glencore was awarded the contract to import 53,000 tonnes of wheat in Bulgaria to be delivered by July 5," Savcheva told a news conference.

The agriculture ministry's wheat and maize import tender on June 5 attracted bids from 28 firms, said Savcheva. Glencore won two previous tenders in March and in May to import a total of 100,000 tonnes of wheat against exports of 131,750 tonnes from this year's crop.
"Glencore proposed the lowest price and the company has met its contractual obligations in the first two tenders," Savcheva said.
Bulgarian private firm Inpro won the tender to import 10,000 tonnes of feed maize. "Inpro proposed the lowest price of $139.70 per tonne of maize to be delivered by July 5," Savcheva said.

Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said in May Bulgaria needs to import 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat and 200,000 tonnes of feed maize to cover a consumption gap until this year's crop and additional 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat before next year's crop.

Uncontrolled exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year caused an acute grain shortage earlier this year. Varbanov said the government would raise minimum purchase grain prices closer to international ones, in a bid to encourage local production.
